note: Symptoms are written as a bug reporter would describe the problem; gold_files are the source files changed by the commit that fixed it (tests, docs and translations excluded). Written before measuring; do not tune them to the tool. Tasks marked set=design were visible while the keyword tier of diagnose_bug was designed; set=held-out tasks were written afterwards from commit titles only and run once. Frozen at version 2: do not edit symptoms or answer keys; add new tasks under a new version. The harness runs each task on its fix_commit's parent (git archive), indexed from that snapshot only.

tasks.symptoms: After changing my key's passphrase, ssh-add keeps retrying the old saved passphrase from the keyring instead of showing the askpass prompt again.
SSH Pilot crashes when I drag a connection in the sidebar and the pointer leaves over the drop gap between two rows. Log shows Gtk-CRITICAL warnings just before the crash.
When a daemon-owned terminal session fails to start, the failure text is also echoed into the terminal itself, so the error appears twice: once in the banner and once as terminal output.
Replies from the daemon reach the GTK window late while it is busy redrawing; results seem to be dispatched at idle priority behind the redraw in the client bridge.
Quitting is blocked with "multiplexed SSH connection could not be checked" whenever the ControlMaster socket check fails transiently.
After upgrading SSH Pilot all my settings were reset to defaults. The old config.json without a current config_version was replaced instead of being migrated.
SFTP downloads from some servers are very slow: when the server answers a READ with fewer bytes than asked, the rest of the chunk is fetched one request at a time.
Add a daemon API for login profiles: list, create, update and delete them over the typed client.
The app feels a bit off sometimes and I am not sure why.
The connection sidebar stays empty or half-built after an exception while the remaining deferred rows are being finished at startup; it never recovers until restart.
Pasting a large block of text into a daemon terminal fails and the terminal stops working instead of receiving the whole paste.
When I quit, open terminals briefly report a failure because the daemon transport was closed, even though quitting is what closed it.
On macOS some clicks are lost, and scrolling with the mouse wheel in the terminal floods the remote shell with input.
On Windows the app hangs at startup when a stale daemon endpoint from a previous run is left behind.
